title: Sights, Sounds, and Atmospheres
grammar: Active present participial modifiers (-ó/-ő) before the noun
goal: I can form active present participles using the -ó/-ő suffix according to vowel harmony.
I can place expanded -ó/-ő participial phrases directly before the head noun.
I can describe sounds, scents, and atmospheric motion in B2 Hungarian.

sections.title: Unit 2: Memory, Nostalgia & Sensory Description
body: Hungarian descriptive prose achieves its lyrical density through left-branching participial clauses (melléknévi igeneves szerkezetek). Where English places relative clauses ('who was sitting by the window', 'which had been forgotten for decades') after the noun, Hungarian packs the entire scene—adverbials, objects, and agents—directly in front of the noun.

Through Gyula Krúdy's atmospheric masterpiece A vörös postakocsi (1913), you will learn how to weave active (-ó/-ő) and anterior/passive (-t/-tt) participial modifiers into lush sensory portraits of turn-of-the-century Pest-Buda.
